text: Grey Market wagons past the Sunken Steeple — salt and nails, fair but sharp. Sarella says pay on time or the road forgets you.
Lantern crows stole the wicks again. The Wayfinder pays buttons for white tail feathers — chart ink wants clean light.
Mara seeks 200 wood — the east wall remembers green timber. She will not lay another course on a twist.
Moth-deer sign in the high clearings. Good luck for a year, says the butcher — or a warning, if you ask Old Bell.
Dren Salt's carters mending the west bridge. Toll is up a nail a wheel. Kess Longaxe takes the other week.
Moon-moths thick on the Grove — a good picking night, say the foragers. Issa wants three moth-wings for the Chart Log.
A poacher tapped the watchfire twice last night. Bread, not chain, says the Mooncleric — and the warning held.
Old Bell's bent clapper still on the market stall. Touch it for luck — one button. Three clacks means the owls have gone quiet.
Bristle boars rooting the south kiln-pads. Mara complains. The butcher smiles. Tomm says rest the pasture a night.
Grey light coming. The builders say grey days set mortar best — Maro's chalk still shows on the Manor sill.
Joren's hat still hangs by the hall door. Nobody touches it. Everybody checks. The Timber Line remembers the tax.
Two knocks answered by two knocks in the treeline. Grandmothers hurry the children home. The Wayfinder marks failed hearths, not ghosts.
The Lantern Towns pay premium for blue-veined timber. Everybody sells. Nobody forgot the winters the road ran empty.
Pond gone dark three nights running? Rest it. Overdrawn land goes pale — Tomm Waterwise will not say it twice.
Pale riders past the west bridge, torches stacked like cordwood. Sorrel counts their fires nightly and chalks the watch roster twice.
Rue's old band drinks at the Sunken Steeple and talks too loud. She left them the bill and kept the map.
Three accounts of the Thinning hang in the Chart Log. Issa will not pick one. She only writes what the living still do.
Mine breathes cold and bright. Assayers call it moonstone; the Mooncleric calls it a debt the hill still pays.
Ashwood crews from two failed clearings. Not hate — arithmetic. Ransom them once and some learn to tap the watchfire twice.
Signal Watchfire still answers a double-tap. The Mooncleric says light steadies; it does not smite.
The Wayfinder marks failed hearths on the Timber Line chart so no one rebuilds on a dry well. Build water first.
Second-Lantern Issa keeps Sella's seed stories and the Chart Log. Beds before bodies still holds.
Ember Road charcoal trails run thin. Sarella of the Forge will not choose which warrior goes short if the coal holds.
No one promises the sun. The Manner keeps one light and mends the rest — that is the whole theology of the hall.
